correctness.rationale: For circular mixed binary w with no cyclic 11 and μ(0)=01, μ(1)=00, the 2|w| cyclic rotations partition strictly by prefixes 000 (even 1), 001 (odd 1), 01 (even 0), 1 (odd 0); preceding characters respectively 1,0,1-w_{i-1},0. In the even-0 block, μ reverses the lexical order of original 0-leading rotations (μ(0)>μ(1)); preceding bits are complemented, giving BWT(μ(w))=1^k 0^k complement(reverse(C(w))) 0^z. Tied rotations (nonprimitive w) contribute identical preceding bits so no ambiguity. All μ iterates avoid 11 cyclic, and C_{m+1}=1^(k_m)0^(k_m) complement(reverse(C_m)), C_1=1, C_2=100. Since the suffix/prefix invariant is 1-start/0-end, each iteration m>=2 adds precisely two runs; terminal zeros merge, yielding r(BWT(W_m))=2m-2 for every m>=2. Direct cyclic-rotation sorting independently confirmed the identity for all 187 mixed no-11 words of lengths 2..9 and every iterate through m=9. The all-length proof is by strict order blocks, not experimental extrapolation.
